title: Translation and Psychometric Validation of the Patient-Reported Apnea Questionnaire (PRAQ) for Assessing Health-Related Quality of Life in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
summary:
The study examines whether the PRAQ‑D, a questionnaire on quality of life in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), works in German just as well as the original version.
OSA is a common condition in which the upper airways collapse repeatedly during sleep. This often leads to disturbed, fragmented sleep, and many affected individuals experience symptoms such as significant daytime fatigue, sleep problems, and sometimes breathlessness. In medical diagnosis and treatment, the focus is mainly on measurable parameters. However, for those affected, it is also crucial to understand how the condition impacts daily life—for example in terms of energy, mood, and everyday functioning. A questionnaire can capture exactly this perspective.
So far, in the German-speaking region there are not enough well‑tested questionnaires for OSA that are completed by patients themselves and can reliably measure how burdensome the condition is. The PRAQ was developed for this purpose. The aim of this study is therefore to evaluate the German translation and determine how well it captures quality of life in a way that is understandable and reliable.
A key question of the study is: Does the PRAQ‑D measure the same aspects just as well as the original version? To answer this, the questionnaire is completed by participants at several time points: first before or at the beginning of treatment, then again after 10–14 days, and finally again after 6–8 weeks, once the therapy is already well established. This makes it possible to assess whether the questionnaire delivers results that are meaningful and stable over time.

interventions.name: Patients receive the German translation of the PRAQ (PRAQ‑D) at three time points, as well as additional questionnaires to assess convergent validity.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients with suspected obstructive sleep apnea requiring treatment
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients in whom there is no OSA requiring treatment.
• Patients who are unable to understand the questionnaire or to answer the questions independently (cognitive impairment).
• Pediatric patients.
• Patients represented by a court-appointed guardian.
• Patients with missing or limited German language proficiency.
